events.title: Carloman dies, leaving Charlemagne sole king of the Franks
events.description: Carloman I, Charlemagne's brother and co-ruler, died suddenly. Charlemagne took over his kingdom, and Carloman's widow fled with her sons to the Lombards.
events.html: Carloman I, Charlemagne's brother and co-ruler, died suddenly. Charlemagne took over his kingdom, and Carloman's widow fled with her sons to the Lombards.

events.title: Louis IX and Henry III make peace in the Treaty of Paris
events.description: Kings Louis IX of France and Henry III of England signed the Treaty of Paris, by which Henry gave up his claims to Normandy, Anjou, Maine and Poitou and held Gascony as a duchy, paying homage for it to the French king.
events.html: Kings Louis IX of France and Henry III of England signed the Treaty of Paris, by which Henry gave up his claims to Normandy, Anjou, Maine and Poitou and held Gascony as a duchy, paying homage for it to the French king.

events.title: Bertrand du Guesclin's French army defeats the English at Pontvallain
events.description: In two separate engagements, a French army of 5,200 men under Bertrand du Guesclin heavily defeated an English force of about the same size, which had broken away from the army of Sir Robert Knolles after a dispute between the commanders.
events.html: In two separate engagements, a French army of 5,200 men under Bertrand du Guesclin heavily defeated an English force of about the same size, which had broken away from the army of Sir Robert Knolles after a dispute between the commanders.

events.title: The Council of Trent holds its final session
events.description: The Council of Trent, which had opened on 13 December 1545, held its final session. Called in response to the Reformation, it had reaffirmed Catholic doctrine on scripture, justification and the seven sacraments and ordered reforms such as seminaries for priests.

events.title: Fifty Christians are burned alive in the Great Martyrdom of Edo
events.description: In Edo, the city now called Tokyo, 50 foreign and domestic Catholics, known as kirishitans, were burned alive for their Christianity. The executions are remembered as the Great Martyrdom of Edo.
events.html: In Edo, the city now called Tokyo, 50 foreign and domestic Catholics, known as kirishitans, were burned alive for their Christianity. The executions are remembered as the Great Martyrdom of Edo.

events.title: Charles XI defeats the invading Danish army at the Battle of Lund
events.description: A Swedish army of about 8,000 under Charles XI defeated a Danish army of some 13,000 under Christian V north of Lund in Scania, in the Scanian War. By casualty percentage it is one of the bloodiest battles ever fought in Scandinavia.
events.html: A Swedish army of about 8,000 under Charles XI defeated a Danish army of some 13,000 under Christian V north of Lund in Scania, in the Scanian War. By casualty percentage it is one of the bloodiest battles ever fought in Scandinavia.

events.title: The Observer is first published
events.description: The first issue of The Observer appeared in London. It is the world's oldest Sunday newspaper still in publication.
events.html: The first issue of The Observer appeared in London. It is the world's oldest Sunday newspaper still in publication.

events.title: The National Grange is founded
events.description: Oliver Kelley and colleagues founded the Order of Patrons of Husbandry, known as the Grange, in Washington. It became a powerful voice for farmers against railway rates and monopolies.
events.html: Oliver Kelley and colleagues founded the Order of Patrons of Husbandry, known as the Grange, in Washington. It became a powerful voice for farmers against railway rates and monopolies.

events.title: The Mary Celeste is found drifting and abandoned
events.description: The crew of the Dei Gratia found the American brigantine Mary Celeste sailing unmanned in the Atlantic, her cargo intact and lifeboat gone. The fate of the ten people aboard has never been explained.
events.html: The crew of the Dei Gratia found the American brigantine Mary Celeste sailing unmanned in the Atlantic, her cargo intact and lifeboat gone. The fate of the ten people aboard has never been explained.

events.title: Pan Am ceases operations
events.description: Pan American World Airways flew its last flight after 64 years. The airline had pioneered transoceanic air travel and launched the Boeing 747, but it never recovered from deregulation, recession and the Lockerbie bombing.

song: German Christians of the late Middle Ages; later Lutheran churches and English-speaking choirs
A Christmas carol from about 1328 that mixes German and Latin. A story says its writer heard angels sing it and danced with them.
